cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers both prior turns: 'You're both forecasting from a chair'; T5 turns T1's rule back on it.
cells.limitation: T7 opens a new growth thread loosely tied to T6's flexibility point.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 adds 'what the money buys', absent from openings; T10 uses it: decide what the raise is for.
cells.limitation: T8's narrowing largely restates T2's prediction worry rather than adding a new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Hours versus money (T1, T5) and forecast versus trial (T3, T4, T11) are examined in depth.
cells.limitation: The current job, its commute and satisfaction, is never raised as the baseline being compared.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 accepts T9's tripwire with a written-down condition; T12 grants T11 yet keeps reversibility disputed.
cells.limitation: T11's quick 'Agreed' adds sharpening but little resistance before the closing turn.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reframes the question as purpose of raise, displaced hours, and reversibility.
cells.limitation: Still-disputed points in D are stated but not sharpened into what would settle them.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 uses the Accountant's own life-cost rule to show money can return life too.
cells.limitation: T4 treats the T3 rehearsal as a full test, slightly stronger than T3 claimed.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the flaw: three novelty mornings cannot show month-nine January darkness; T9 answers with a tripwire.
cells.limitation: T7's 'flexibility is a hope' objection goes unanswered by the Experimenter in later turns.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 arithmetic holds: 3 hours x ~235 workdays = ~700; $20,000/700 = ~$28.
cells.limitation: Basis fields in T1, T4, T7, T10 cite the 'Economy' chapter from a non-browsing worker.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T8: 'that's about averages. It can't tell you whether you're the person'.
cells.limitation: T8 states commute non-adaptation as research findings without signalling it lies outside the cited book.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T12: 'Granted, the trial is imperfect' concedes T4 and T11 while narrowing its own claim.
cells.limitation: T8 narrows its earlier claim without naming which argument prompted the narrowing.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A treats 'how do I decide' as a method question and lists decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: Never asks why the user sought or is weighing this offer at all.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 turns 90 minutes each way into ~700 hours a year and an hourly price.
cells.limitation: T1's $20,000 raise is a hypothetical, not derived from the user's salary.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T10 and section D ask the user to name what the raise is for.
cells.limitation: User's priorities stay unknown; speakers' values (Thoreau's life-cost) frame the ledger by default.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T4 names displaced dinner, sleep, exercise and whoever waits at home.
cells.limitation: Commute money cost (fuel, fares) is mentioned once in T1 and never weighed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on raise purpose, remote days, driving versus train, and reversibility.
cells.limitation: The user's current commute length, which sets the real time delta, is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 offers debt or runway as possible purposes of the raise, framed conditionally.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives for considering the move (escape, status, growth) offered as a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 exposes the assumption that a vivid paycheck outweighs a dull commute.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the current job is the stable default is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T4 'Ask what each hour displaces, not just what it earns' sets time against income.
cells.limitation: No point asks which displaced activity the user would most refuse to lose.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 and T10 name dread of the route and month-four rationalization without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Obligation, household expectations, or fear of refusing more money are never explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D ends with a one-sentence test the user can answer or reject.
cells.limitation: Only one reflective question is posed; most branches are conditions rather than questions.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options span accept, decline, counter (T6), and accept with written tripwire (T9, T10).
cells.limitation: Moving closer to the new job is never named as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T7 weighs commute hours against growth; T12 weighs trial against job-hunting cost.
cells.limitation: T6's counteroffer is presented without its risk of losing or souring the offer.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: remote days, train versus drive, named raise purpose, reversibility, each with favoured option.
cells.limitation: T9's month-four tripwire and T6's 20% counter are numbers not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T11 separates what a trial can reveal from risk unknowable until lived.
cells.limitation: Unknowns in A are listed flat; none is ranked above another in the debate.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Ride the route at rush hour, ask about flexibility in writing, write the exit rule beforehand.
cells.limitation: No step to compute the actual raise against the user's own salary.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 'the price tag nobody printed' states the cost idea in plain terms.
cells.limitation: T4 'Rehearsals flatter' is compressed enough to need a second reading.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T9 'my case for the rehearsal' points clearly back to T3.
cells.limitation: T8 'my earlier claim' could mean T2 or T5.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within range per deterministic checks, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: Turns cluster at similar lengths, giving an even, slightly metronomic pace.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Accountant prices hours, Skeptic doubts forecasts, Experimenter proposes trials; positions stay distinct.
cells.limitation: All three share one brisk, aphoristic register; voices differ more in stance than style.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E condenses the debate into four branches without re-arguing turns.
cells.limitation: The 700-hours figure recurs in T1, T10 and E with little new use.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T4 makes hours concrete: dinner, sleep, whoever is waiting at home.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay generic since the user's life details are unknown and not imagined vividly.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T10 accepts T9's tripwire after T9 argued averages cannot settle the individual case.
cells.limitation: T8's narrowing names no cause; T10 does not say what changed the Accountant's mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: Thoreau's Accountant prices life in hours with a dry edge: 'a steep price for an unlabeled number'.
cells.limitation: The Skeptic and Experimenter speak in near-identical crisp registers.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3 'forecasting from a chair'; T4 'January darkness in month nine'.
cells.limitation: Closing turns T11 and T12 are functional rather than striking.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: Tension rises from T4's challenge to T9's tripwire and T12's unresolved reversibility.
cells.limitation: Even turn lengths and steady intensity give little variation in rhythm across T1 to T12.

strengths: T5 turns the Accountant's own life-cost rule against T1's ledger, and T10 builds on it.
Section E gives observable branches (remote days, train vs drive, raise purpose, reversibility) with favoured options.
T4 and T11 test the Experimenter's trial on a named assumption; T12 concedes and narrows.
weaknesses: Basis fields in T1, T4, T7, T10 cite a chapter from a worker that could not browse.
No mind raises the current job or moving closer as the baseline and an option.
Motives and fears behind the move get one question (section D), no alternatives offered.

symptoms.observed: Basis fields cite a specific chapter though the worker could not browse.
Current job's commute and satisfaction never enter the comparison.
symptoms.evidence: Three hours a day is roughly 700 hours a year

symptoms.observed: Options cover counter and tripwire but never relocating closer.
symptoms.evidence: A counter of 20% with Fridays at home might beat

symptoms.observed: Raise purposes offered; no alternative motives for considering the move posed as question.
symptoms.evidence: A raise that clears debt or buys a year of runway

symptoms.observed: Trial length and tripwire date are numbers not drawn from the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: if by month four you dread the route

findings.location: Basis fields of T1, T4, T7, T10
findings.description: Basis fields name the 'Economy' chapter of Walden though the worker could not browse; deterministic check reports 4.
Claim that people adapt poorly to commutes is presented under Kahneman's book; it likely draws on other commuting research.
pd=true quotation from Walden matches the evaluator's memory of the text but is not confirmed here.

rubric_fit_notes: The chapter citation is to a real chapter and the quotation in T1 appears accurate from memory, so it was treated as a material C2.3 weakness, not a cap reason.
With only two user facts, C3 and C4 depend mostly on questions and branches.
